Name: Requiring the department of buildings to inform property owners of permit sign-off requirements.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to requiring the department of buildings to inform property owners of permit sign-off requirements

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Housing and Buildings
This Introduction was Hearing Held by Committee
This Introduction was Laid Over by Committee

Summary: This bill would require the Department of Buildings (“DOB”) to notify property owners with open permits that the permits must receive DOB sign-off. DOB would be required to email an initial notice within 7 days of the issuance of a permit, with such notice informing property owners of the consequences of failing to obtain sign-off alongside instructions for accessing DOB’s online self-service portal. This bill would require DOB to send follow-up notifications 2 months after the expiration of a permit and 6 months after the expiration of a permit if such permit has not been renewed and yet to receive sign-off within 30 days of such expiration. Finally, this bill would also require DOB to develop a resource guide on sign-off requirements, with such guide posted to the department’s website.
Text:
A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to requiring the department of buildings to inform property owners of permit sign-off requirements

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Article 116 of chapter 1 of title 28 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new section 28-116.8 to read as follows:
§ 28-116.8 Notification to owner about sign-off requirements. Within 7 days of the issuance of a permit, the commissioner shall provide the owner with written notice regarding sign-off requirements. The commissioner shall provide such notice by electronic mail. The notice shall:

1. Provide the permit number and the expiration date of the permit;

2. Explain that sign-off is required pursuant to section 28-116.4 and describe the requirements for obtaining sign-off, including the website address of the department’s sign-off resource guide developed pursuant to section 28-116.8.2;

3. Explain that construction or work must remain accessible for required inspections in accordance with section 28-116.1, and that if work is sealed behind a wall or made otherwise inaccessible prior to completion of a required inspection, it may be necessary to remove the wall or otherwise make the work accessible to allow for inspection;

4. Describe the consequences of failing to obtain sign-off, including the need to renew expired permits and pay reinstatement fees, the impact on the issuance of future permits at the property, and the impact on the ability to sell or obtain financing for the property; 

5. Provide instructions for accessing the department’s online self-service portal; 

6. Explain that failure to receive any additional notifications from the department regarding the sign-off of the permit does not eliminate or otherwise affect the obligation of an owner to obtain sign-off; and

7. Include any other information the commissioner deems relevant. 

§ 28-116.8.1 Sign-off requirements reminders. When work for which a permit is required has not received sign-off pursuant to section 28-116.4 within 30 days after the expiration of such permit, and such permit has not been renewed, the commissioner shall provide the owner with written notice that the work has not received sign-off. Such notice shall be provided by electronic mail no later than 2 months after the expiration of such permit. Unless the department has documented sign-off of such work, a second notice shall be provided by electronic mail no later than 6 months after the expiration of such permit. Each such notice shall include the website address of the department’s sign-off resource guide developed pursuant to section 28-116.8.2 and the contact information for the department’s office located in the same borough as the property. 

§ 28-116.8.2 Sign-off resource guide. The department shall develop and maintain a resource guide of sign-off requirements. The department shall post such guide on the department’s website and regularly update information provided in such guide as necessary. 

§ 2. This local law takes effect 180 days after it becomes law.
